title: State AGs fight Character AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats
lede: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is trying to stop bankrupt Character.ai from auctioning user data, including private chat histories, after it told users their information would not be sold.

points: The AGs say the dataset spans more than 21 million US accounts, over 2.1 million of them minors, plus data such as IP addresses.
Character.ai filed for Chapter 11 in October, and the auction is set for December 1.
The only disclosed bidder, Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, was formed in Delaware on November 13 and named the base bid a day later.
The AGs argue a buyer could resell the data freely and would not be bound by Character.ai's privacy policy.
Chatbot safety laws in several states take effect January 1, 2027, which the sale could also breach.

sections.text: Chat logs are turning into an asset in AI bankruptcies, and regulators are testing whether privacy promises survive a sale. Anyone storing user conversations should expect those promises to be enforced.
